newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister to quit in government row - agency.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister to quit in government row - agency.

text.p: A Turkish minister from the conservative wing of the Islamist-led coalition said on Saturday he was to resign in a government dispute over implementation of anti-Islamist military demands, Anatolian news agency said.
"Trade and Industry Minister Yalim Erez said he will present his resignation to Prime Minister (Necmettin) Erbakan," Anatolian said.

"Out of respect for myself and the Turkish people I will give my resignation to the prime minister," Erez was quoted as saying after 30 minutes of talks with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, his party leader.

Erez and another minister from the True Path Party had already expressed open opposition to the Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party for stalling on military demands for a crackdown on religious activism.

Turkey's powerful National Security Council was to meet later on Saturday to discuss the implementation of military demands for restrictions on religious education, penalising Islamist dress and moving against Islamist business and media.
Ciller denied on Friday she would pull out of the coalition.
